sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Medical Device FDA 510(k) Filing and European CE Mark Compliance

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - federal constitutional monarchy; British Columbia is a common law province; Quebec private law is civil law; no sharia
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA; entered into force 1 Oct 2014)
Canada-China Income Tax Agreement (1986, effective for taxation years commencing 1987)
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the EU/EEA member states
Agreement between Canada, the United States and Mexico (USMCA/CUSMA/T-MEC), Chapter 14

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 462.3; Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), SBC 2002, c 57, ss 22-25, 119-122 and Part 7; BC transparency register rules; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Magnitsky Act), SC 2017, c 21

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized declaration of ultimate beneficial ownership and control structure (UBO chart)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or licensed lawyer in the beneficial owner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for all current and former Hague Convention states) OR Consular Legalization (non-Hague states; e.g., notarial and foreign consular chain)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of government-issued passport / identity card of each UBO and named director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office or national identity-issuing authority of each UBO/director

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / certificate of corporate status for any corporate shareholder (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or equivalent competent authority of each corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or professional legal/accounting reference letter for promoter/UBO due diligence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank, auditor, or regulated professional relying on client due diligence requirements
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (original letter must be notarized if the bank's signature is not otherwise verifiable)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of UBOs, directors and authorized signatories against: (i) UN Consolidated List; (ii) OFAC SDN List; (iii) Canadian regulations under Special Economic Measures Act, Magnitsky Act, and United Nations Act; (iv) FINTRAC guidance on politically exposed persons (PEPs) and heads of international organizations; enhanced due diligence for PEPs; suspicious transaction reporting to FINTRAC within prescribed timelines; record retention for at least 5 years after account or relationship closes.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registry Services - Name Request Online / OneStop Business Registry (onestop.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in Latin characters and must include a recognized legal element ('Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated' or BC statutory variants). A Chinese or other non-Latin corporate name may be accepted only in transliterated or English form; BC does not register Chinese-character names as the legal corporate name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A BC Name Request cannot be administratively extended beyond 56 days; if incorporation is not completed, a new Name Request must be submitted. Upon rejection, the applicant (1) receives the Registrar's refusal reasons; (2) should revise the name to add a distinguishing element, or remove/obtain consent for a prohibited/sensitive token; (3) may submit a written request to BC Registry Services for reconsideration of the refusal; and (4) only in exceptional cases may seek judicial review before the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for MedTech regulatory consulting: a BC statutory registered office may be a commercial virtual office if it is a real, physical street address in BC at which process can be served and records may be inspected; a post-office box or shared mail drop is insufficient.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - approximately 5% annual likelihood. BC Registry generally does not conduct routine physical inspections for low-risk consulting companies; unannounced inspections are reserved for reasonable suspicion of unlawful activity, AML/CFT non-compliance, or court-ordered investigation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: BC Name Approval / Name Request Fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: BC Registry Services / Director under Business Corporations Act
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Published BC corporate registry tariff of CAD 30.00

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO/AML due diligence and sanctions screening (PEP, OFAC, UN, Canada SEMA/Magnitsky) for three individuals
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Engaged corporate services provider or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark flat fee for low-risk MedTech consulting company

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of UBO declarations, passport copies and corporate shareholder certificates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in Canada or in foreign jurisdiction of document origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark notary fee; no universal statutory tariff in British Columbia

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of pre-incorporation document bundle (at least four documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Global Affairs Canada (Authentication Services) or foreign consulate/embassy
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Global Affairs Canada CAD 15.00 per authentication document; foreign consular fees according to published schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial virtual registered office and records address in British Columbia (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for BC physical registered-office plus records-address service

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: British Columbia Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57 (BCBCA), ss. 10-21 (incorporation), ss. 32-41 (corporate records), ss. 99-118 (share capital), and ss. 173-200 (directors and officers); Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44 (available for federal incorporation but not elected for this BC provincial filing); Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. I-5 as amended (tax registrations ancillary to incorporation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services – Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia (corporateonline.gov.bc.ca); postal: PO Box 9431 Stn Prov Govt, Victoria, BC V8W 9V3
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles (Form 1) and Articles (Form 2) filed under the BCBCA; the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation as conclusive evidence of the company's existence.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no capital escrow requirement under the BCBCA; a nominal subscription (e.g., 1 common share per incorporator at CAD $1 par value) is sufficient. Consideration for shares may be paid in money, property, or past services; the directors must determine the fair value of non-cash consideration and record it in the share subscription ledger.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The first directors, constituting a quorum, approve the issuance of 100 common shares to each incorporator upon receipt of full subscription proceeds; the registered office of the Company shall be fixed at the registered address set out in the Notice of Articles and the Notice of Articles be filed with the BC Registrar; [First Name] [Last Name] is appointed President and Director; [Second Name] [Last Name] is appointed Secretary-Treasurer and Director; [Third Name] [Last Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until successors are elected; the corporate seal is adopted and the minute book, share registers and share certificates are established; the officers are authorized to open a corporate bank account and execute all ancillary filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services – Name Reservation Portal (bcregistries.gov.bc.ca) / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (NUANS report supplier)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) pre-approved name report through an approved service provider, or submit a name request directly through BC Corporate Online. Choose a corporate name ending in 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', 'Holdings', or other prescribed legal element. Pay the name reservation fee (CAD $30) and retain the Name Reservation Statement, which is valid for 56 days. Verify the name against both BC corporate records and federal trademark records before processing the incorporation.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report (or online name request printout)
Proposed corporate name options (primary and up to 3 alternates)
Government-issued photo identification of the name applicant/officer
Contact information and email address for notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects or conditions the name, file a revised Name Request within the 56-day reservation window; obtain consent from the existing trademark holder or adjust the corporate name. Request reconsideration through BC Registries contact center (1-877-526-1526) with a corrected Name Status Report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Articles and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate legal counsel / BC Corporate Online filing platform; registered office must be physically located in British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Notice of Articles (Form 1) identifying the company's full legal name, notice address, registered office address in BC, share structure (classes, special rights) and first directors. Draft the Articles (Form 2) covering the incorporating subscribers, business restrictions, share classes, director liability exclusions, transfer restrictions and any special provisions permitted under the BCBCA. Have each incorporator and a witness sign both documents; obtain the signed consent of each first director and consent of the registered office service provider (if any).
required_dossiers: Notice of Articles (Form 1) executed by incorporator and witness
Articles (Form 2) executed by incorporator and witness
Consent to act as first director (Form 3) or director list in Articles
Consent to act as registered office (Form 13) if using a service address
Letter of authorization from the filing agent (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a form contains defective wording, improper share class expressivity, or missing signature, the Registry will return the filing; correct and re-execute the form, obtain fresh signatures and witnesses, and resubmit. BC Registries generally requires processing within 90 days of initial drafting to avoid cancellation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Incorporation Filing and Obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance (online filing via BC Corporate Online at corporateonline.gov.bc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to BC Corporate Online using a BCeID or POST account and submit the incorporation application with the endorsed Notice of Articles and Articles. Pay the incorporation fee (CAD $350 online, approximately USD $260). Upon satisfactory compliance review, the Registrar files the documents and issues a Certificate of Incorporation. Download and verify the Certificate, Notice of Articles, and incorporation particulars; maintain these instruments in the corporate minute book as conclusive proof of formation.
required_dossiers: Electronic incorporation application (Form 10) completed in Corporate Online
Notice of Articles (Form 1)
Articles (Form 2)
Proof of payment (fee receipt)
BCeID/POST login credentials and authorization for the filer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried, the registry provides a deficiency letter identifying the missing information; remedy within 30 days by submitting an amendment to the articles or a revised Notice of Articles. If the application is entirely refused, an appeal may be made to the Registrar via email at BCRegistries@gov.bc.ca with a statutory declaration supporting the corrected filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold Organizational Meeting and Adopt First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First board of directors of the corporation (BCBCA ss. 22 and 224); corporate records maintained at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting of the first directors immediately following incorporation (or in lieu of a meeting, obtain signed written consent of all directors). Adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution approving share subscriptions and issuance of share certificates, confirmation of the registered office, appointment of officers, adoption of the corporate by-laws/seal, and banking resolutions. Complete the corporate minute book, including the register of directors, register of shareholders, share certificate ledger, and transfers register. Issue share certificates and record the consideration in the share subscription ledger.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and endorsed Notice of Articles
Draft First Board Resolution and waiver of notice / written consent
Register of directors' names, addresses and consent forms
Share subscription agreements, funds ledger and share certificates
Minute book with corporate by-laws and resolution documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any director is unable to act or a conflict of interest is declared, have the concerned director execute a disclosure under BCBCA s. 147 and abstain from voting; replace the director by special resolution if the declared interest materially affects the vote. Any failure to retain corporate records may be cured by immediately restoring registers in compliance with BCBCA ss. 32-41.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Federal Business Number and Income Tax Accounts with CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO) at canada.ca and Business Number Registration (Form RC1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, register the corporation with the CRA for a federal Business Number (BN) either online through BRO or by mailing Form RC1. The BN is required for corporate income tax returns, GST/HST account (if making taxable supplies in Canada), payroll source deductions (if hiring employees), and any excise/import-export account. Review the 15-character program accounts and determine whether CRA authorization is needed for representatives (RepID). Start the corporate income tax account by filing the T2 Summary Corporation Income Tax Return for each taxation year and ensure director/officer information is current in the BN system.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles
Officers'/directors' government-issued identification
Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or electronic BRO application
Business mailing address and registered office address in BC
Bank account details for CRA direct debit (if electing electronic payments)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA cannot validate the BN against the BC registry (mismatch of legal name), verify the name and address on Notice of Articles with BC Registries, correct the BC record via a Notice of Change, and resubmit the RC1. To recover an outdated access code, call CRA Business Enquiries at 1-800-959-5525 to obtain a new Activation Code or register a new RepID account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Provincial Accounts, WorkSafeBC and Municipal Business Licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: WorkSafeBC (workers' compensation); BC Ministry of Finance (Employer Health Tax); local municipal business licence office (e.g., City of Vancouver or City of Victoria)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the medical device regulatory consulting company will engage employees in BC, register the firm with WorkSafeBC online at worksafebc.com within three months of the first hire (annual payroll and activity classification apply). Register for Employer Health Tax with the BC Ministry of Finance once annual BC payroll exceeds CAD $1,000,000 (currently no EHT below that threshold). Obtain a municipal business licence from the municipality where the registered office or physical consulting suite is located; provide the Notice of Articles, lease or occupancy certificate, and payment of the applicable licence fee. No sector-specific provincial licence is required for ISIC 7490 regulatory consulting.
required_dossiers: WorkSafeBC registration form (with company legal name, BC incorporation certificate)
Employer Health Tax registration data and payroll estimate (if deductible)
Municipal business licence application and zoning/occupancy approval
Proof of office address (lease or property use certificate)
Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles (for officials verifying status)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a municipality requires a development variance or additional zoning clearance, file the zoning application promptly with the local planning department and request an interim business license or temporary permit. If WorkSafeBC or BC Finance issues an erroneous assessment, file a written notice of objection within 60 days attaching the assessment and supporting payroll records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – ISIC 7490 (FDA 510(k) filing and CE Mark regulatory consulting) is an office-based professional service and is not a reviewable industrial undertaking in British Columbia. If the company later expands into medical device manufacturing, importation or distribution, Health Canada's Medical Devices Bureau (Medical Devices Regulations, SOR/98-282) and the BC Ministry of Health must be engaged as competent authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial or manufacturing operating licence applies to the consulting scope. The only operational permit needed is a municipal business licence (e.g., City of Vancouver Business Licence) for the office premises; a health product establishment licence would be required only if the company physically handles or distributes medical devices.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy – Environmental Assessment Office (EAO)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – professional consulting activities are not a 'reviewable project' under the Environmental Assessment Act, S.B.C. 2018, c. 7. Should the company establish any physical manufacturing or disposal operation in the future, a project notification and likely full EIA (if thresholds are met) would be triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for office operations: zero industrial wastewater discharge and zero VOC/stack emissions. Where applicable to incidental office activity, comply with municipal sewer by-law discharge standards under the BC Municipalities Act, the BC Hazardous Waste Regulation (BC Reg. 63/88) for e-waste and batteries, and CEPA 1999 (SOR/2019-326) GHG reporting thresholds should any combustion generator or freight activities be introduced.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire safety certification and occupancy permit under the BC Fire Code; structural load/occupancy compliance under the BC Building Code for the leased office; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance for desk-based and remote consulting employees (ergonomic evaluation, emergency exit plan, first aid kit); building insurance and business interruption continuity plan maintained as standard professional practice.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; online tax account portal is 'My Business Account'. Provincial parallel authority: British Columbia Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch, accessible via the BC Taxpayer Portal, administers the 7% Provincial Sales Tax (PST) independently of CRA. The federal GST/HST is exclusively administered by CRA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the BC Business Corporations Act; the corporate registry transmits incorporation data to CRA via the integrated OneStop Business Registry, which issues the 9-digit Business Number (BN) automatically. (2) Activate the CRA Business Number and enrol for the mandatory program accounts: Corporate Income Tax (RC), GST/HST (RT), and Payroll (RP) via the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal or by calling the CRA Business Window (1-800-959-5525). (3) If the corporation was incorporated provincially in another province and carries on business in BC, file an extra-provincial registration with BC Corporate Online; no separate tax ID is created. (4) Open a BC PST account only if the company makes PST-taxable sales; professional MedTech regulatory consulting services are not PST-taxable. (5) Appoint an authorized representative by filing Form RC59 to enable third-party tax accountants to file electronically. (6) Obtain the BN confirmation letter containing the taxpayer PIN within 10 business days; non-resident directors are permitted and do not delay issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the Business Corporation is a fully separate taxable person with limited liability and is not pass-through eligible. A resident Canadian corporation is taxed on worldwide income under Part I of the Income Tax Act (IT Act); no territorial scope carve-out applies to BC-headquartered corporations. Tax_Exempt_Zone status does not apply anywhere in mainland Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a 'check-the-box' entity election. Applicable statutory elections: (1) Voluntary registration as a GST/HST small supplier before exceeding the threshold (ETA s. 240); (2) Closely related corporation joint election treating inter-corporate taxable supplies as nil for GST/HST purposes (ETA s. 156); (3) Quick Method accounting election for eligible small businesses; (4) BC PST vendor election to treat sales exclusively for resale as exempt; (5) A US check-the-box election could be filed with the IRS to treat the Canadian corporation as a disregarded entity, which creates hybrid entity exposure and must be reviewed against Canada's anti-hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.4-18.6) to avoid denial of deductions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (federal Goods and Services Tax) plus BC PST (Provincial Sales Tax); British Columbia has never adopted the HST, so there is no harmonized provincial component. The corporation must register and charge 5% GST; BC PST of 7% does not apply to scientific/technical regulatory consulting services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (worldwide taxable supplies of goods and services over any 12-month rolling period; once exceeded, mandatory registration with CRA for GST/HST. BC PST registration is separately triggered only if the business makes PST-taxable sales of enumerated goods or specified professional services; this corporation's consulting output is outside the PST tax base).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government API pre-approval of invoices. Mandatory requirements: invoices must be issued at the time of supply and contain the supplier's name, trading name, BN, date, recipient identity, rate, tax amount, and a 'zero-rated' notation for exports (ETA s. 221). GST/HST returns must be filed electronically by registrants with worldwide revenue exceeding CAD 10 million; paper filing is permitted below that threshold. Books and records, including electronic invoices, must be retained in machine-readable format and kept in Canada for audit (ETA s. 286; ITA ss. 230 and 230.1). A voluntary PEPPOL-based e-invoicing pilot is available but no clearance stamp or SOAP/API accreditation is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Schedule VI, section 9 of the Excise Tax Act: a supply of a service made to a non-resident recipient is taxable at 0% if the recipient is not registered for GST/HST and is not carrying on a commercial activity in Canada at the time of supply, unless the service relates to real property situated in Canada or to tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed. MedTech regulatory consulting (FDA 510(k) filings and CE Mark / ISO 13485 dossiers) is performed in BC for non-resident medical device manufacturers, has no connection to Canadian situs property, and therefore qualifies as zero-rated. The exporter must demonstrate via contractual terms, delivery records, and foreign-currency settlement that the recipient and the place of commercial activity are offshore; invoicing a foreign address alone is insufficient to sustain a zero-rating claim on audit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Signed consulting agreement identifying the non-resident recipient's legal name, registered address, and country of tax residence
Commercial invoice issued in CAD, USD, or EUR with express notation 'Zero-rated export supply - Schedule VI, s. 9 ETA'
Foreign-currency payment evidence, including bank MT103 wire confirmations, SWIFT remittance records, or credit-card gateway settlement reports from foreign issuers
Milestone completion certificate or deliverables acceptance report identifying the offshore principal and confirming no direct link to Canadian real property or Canadian-situs tangible goods
CBSA export declaration (Form B13A) applicable only if physical test samples or regulatory specimens cross the border; pure IP and consulting deliverables require no customs entry
CRA Form GST106 (GST/HST Paid on Taxable Purchases) retained with the file to substantiate full input-tax-credit recovery against zero-rated output
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no formal statutory deadline that requires physical FX repatriation within 180 days; the 180-day window is used as an administrative benchmark for export documentation freshness, and unrepatriated receivables must nonetheless be translated and accrued in Canadian dollars in the year earned. CRA audit scrutiny is elevated for consulting registrants whose input-tax-credit claims exceed the 5% net tax on domestic supplies; where export zero-rating documentation fails, CRA may claw back all claimed ITCs, deny zero-rated treatment retrospectively, and assess: (1) 25% of the net tax deficiency as a misstatement penalty (ETA s. 281.1); (2) 200% of the evaded tax for knowingly false statements (ETA s. 280); (3) criminal fines up to CAD 1,000,000 and imprisonment (ETA s. 327); and (4) a separate 40% penalty on evaded BC PST if the PST exemption is misapplied. Reassessment periods are normally four years, extended to ten years where misrepresentation or fraud is established; corrections can be mitigated through CRA's Voluntary Disclosures Program before audit contact.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary authority; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervises Schedule I chartered banks under the Bank Act; FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada) administers the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and receives Large Electronic Funds Transfer Reports and Large Cash Transaction Reports; the Department of Finance Canada is responsible for exchange-rate and capital-flow policy. Canada operates no restrictive Foreign Exchange Administration: FX transactions are executed freely through federally regulated banking entities, and no prior central-bank approval is required for payments, capital flows, or corporate account opening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CAD is fully convertible on both the current account and the capital account for residents and non-residents. There are no exchange-control permits, no prior-approval gates for profit remittance, and no convertibility limitations. Dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are subject to Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (statutory 25%, reduced by applicable treaty; under the Canada-US Convention generally 5% for a US corporate shareholder owning at least 10% of the voting stock, 15% otherwise; interest typically 0%; royalties 0%-10%), and require the payer to file NR4 returns and obtain treaty-residency documentation (NR301/NR302) before remittance. Cross-border consulting fees paid by a Canadian corporation to non-resident contractors are generally not subject to Part XIII withholding if no Canadian permanent establishment exists, but transfer-pricing documentation under section 247 of the Income Tax Act is required where related parties are involved. For exported consulting services (US FDA 510(k) and EU CE Mark advisory work), GST/HST is zero-rated under the Excise Tax Act, Schedule VI, Part V, Section 7, provided the non-resident recipient is outside Canada and the service is not connected to Canadian real property or goods. No Bank of Canada authorization is required to convert or remit profits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report under the Business Corporations Act (BCBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: British Columbia Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after each annual anniversary of incorporation (annual report date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100 (approx. USD 73) in addition to the annual report fee; continued failure to file for two consecutive annual report periods leads to administrative dissolution by the Registrar; reinstatement requires court application and payment of all arrears and reinstatement fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the balance owing payable by the due date, plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; for repeated late filings, the base penalty is 10% plus 2% per month. Certificates of non-filing and potential tax defaults may be registered with the Federal Court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Final Return for the Fiscal Period (where not monthly/quarterly)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year end for annual GST/HST filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid net GST/HST plus 1% per month up to 12 months; repeated failures are penalized at 10% plus 2% per month. Interest accumulates on overdue amounts; continued non-filing may trigger mandatory electronic filing and higher penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the BC Business Corporations Act, distribution to the public and reporting-issuer status trigger mandatory audited financial statements. A private BC company is generally exempt from an annual independent audit unless its articles or a unanimous shareholder agreement require one, or shareholders holding at least 5% of the issued voting shares pass a resolution requiring audited financial statements. Federally incorporated CBCA corporations may be required to appoint an auditor in similar circumstances; no specific asset or revenue threshold applies for BC private corporations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises; private BC corporations may choose IFRS or Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises, Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook). Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with Canadian GAAP for tax, regulatory, and creditor purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: BC provincial companies must maintain a share register and directors register updated contemporaneously on any share transfer or director change; no standalone UBO annual filing is currently mandated for ordinary non-land-owning BC private corporations. For companies incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act, an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register must be maintained and updated within 15 days of a change in significant control; annual confirmation of the ISC register is made in the federal annual return. BC companies holding land must maintain a transparency register under the Land Ownership Transparency Act and file the mandated transparency report. Management should reconcile the register of members with all current shareholder and UBO records on each corporate anniversary.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined federal and British Columbia general corporate income tax rate (15% federal + 12% BC)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction reduces the federal rate to 9% and the BC small business rate to 2% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income, producing a combined 11% small business rate. No statutory tax holiday applies to FDA 510(k) or CE Mark regulatory consulting. Eligible Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) expenditures may generate refundable investment tax credits (35% for Canadian-controlled private corporations, 15% non-refundable for other corporations). BC capital investment and regional tax credits may apply only if qualifying capital expenditures and eligible activities are established.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; BC corporate income tax is administered by the Canada Revenue Agency through the T2 and integrated provincial schedules, including Schedule 5 (Provincial and Territorial Taxes and Credits); electronic filing is mandatory for most corporations and is completed through CRA-certified E-file tax preparation software or the CRA's secure e-services.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporations pay corporate income tax instalments monthly or quarterly in the taxation year if federal and provincial tax payable exceeds CAD 3,000; GST/HST and payroll remittances are filed separately on their own frequency.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return must be filed no later than six months after the end of the corporation's fiscal period. The balance-due day for corporate income tax is generally two months after the fiscal year-end, extended to three months for Canadian-controlled private corporations eligible for the small business deduction. Instalments and final payment are tied to the balance-due day, not the filing deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal corporate name, 9-digit Business Number (BN), jurisdiction of incorporation, registered office address, and mailing address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact legal name as registered in the home jurisdiction. If the corporation has no BN, apply for a BN through the CRA; declare the foreign jurisdiction of incorporation and Canadian permanent establishment positions accurately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 - Province or Territory of Taxation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Select British Columbia if the corporation has a permanent establishment in BC and is subject to BC corporate income tax allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation must determine whether a permanent establishment exists in BC under the federal-BC allocation treaty and allocate income using the BC Schedule 5 rules if it carries on business through a fixed place of business or dependent agent in BC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the last day of the taxation year; the fiscal period cannot exceed 53 weeks and must be consistent with the financial statements used for tax reporting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation's Canadian taxation year may be deemed by the CRA to be a calendar year if books and records are not maintained in Canada; ensure the fiscal year-end is consistently supported by board resolutions and accounting records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 10 - Gross Revenue / Regulatory Consulting Fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from FDA 510(k) filing assistance, CE marking technical documentation, ISO 13485 gap assessments, post-market surveillance, and regulatory strategy consulting before deducting expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source revenue and, where services are rendered partly outside Canada, follow the CRA's source rules and any applicable tax treaty nexus provisions. Fee-for-service revenue is generally taxable if the services are performed in Canada or if a Canadian permanent establishment exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue less deductible overhead, salaries, rent, professional fees, capital cost allowance, and non-capital loss carryovers; this is the tax base for federal and BC corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations may deduct expenses to the extent they are reasonable and incurred to earn Canadian-source income. Expenses incurred for foreign operations must be allocated appropriately; transfer pricing adjustments must be made for non-arm's-length charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 60 - Net Tax Payable / Part XIV Branch Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax at 15% or 9% and BC tax at 12% or 2%, reduced by refundable and non-refundable credits and instalments. For non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada, the additional Part XIV branch tax of 25% applies to unremitted Canadian-source taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the Part XIV branch tax calculation for a Canadian permanent establishment. Dividends paid out of Canadian branch earnings to foreign shareholders remain subject to Part XIII withholding except where treaty relief is available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax, plus 1% per complete month late to a maximum of 12 months; a repeat failure raises the base penalty to 10% and the monthly surcharge to 2% to a maximum of 20 months. The CRA charges daily compound interest on unpaid balances at the prescribed rate plus applicable federal and provincial income tax. Failure to file Form T106 or to prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation can trigger separate penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act on dividends paid or credited by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder; BC imposes no separate dividend withholding tax and the 25% rate may be reduced under an applicable tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced treaty withholding, the non-resident payee must complete Form NR301 (Declaration of Entitlement to Benefits Under a Tax Treaty) and provide it to the Canadian payer before the payment is made. The payee must also obtain and provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of its country of residence. The payer should retain the NR301 and TRC for audit purposes. If the full 25% withholding has been remitted, the non-resident recipient must file Form NR7-R (Application for Refund of Non-Resident Tax Withheld) with the CRA within the applicable statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for IP, trademarks, know-how, technical assistance, and regulatory process documents are subject to the statutory 25% Part XIII withholding tax, reducible under tax treaties to rates typically between 0% and 15%. Interest paid to non-arm's-length non-resident creditors is subject to the statutory 25% withholding tax, while interest paid at arm's length is generally exempt from Part XIII; treaty benefits may further reduce or eliminate related-party interest withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 in total annual fair market value of reportable transactions with each non-arm's-length non-resident triggers mandatory Form T106 filing and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation. Multinational groups with consolidated global revenue of at least CAD 750,000,000 must file Country-by-Country (CbC) reporting with the CRA.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime, but the CRA may ignore, recharacterize, or adjust transactions under section 247 and the section 245 General Anti-Avoidance Rule if a BC consulting corporation lacks real economic substance. A BC corporation providing FDA 510(k) and CE Mark services must maintain a physical office, qualified professional employees, board oversight, client contracts, technical manuals, project records, invoicing, and bank accounts in BC to prove real business risk, decisions, and operational substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion and False Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully underreporting FDA/CE consulting fees, creating fictitious subcontractor invoices, inflating deductible expenses, or making false statements on the T2 return or Form T106 to the CRA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Gross negligence penalty under section 163(2) of the Income Tax Act equal to 50% of the tax understated; criminal prosecution under subsection 239(1) may result in a fine of between 50% and 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment for up to five years. The CRA may also reassess beyond the normal reassessment period where misrepresentation is due to neglect, fraud, or wilful default.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who direct, authorize, or participate in evasion are personally exposed to criminal charges, fines, restitution to the CRA, imprisonment, and travel restrictions as a condition of bail or criminal proceedings. The corporate veil may be pierced where the corporation is a facade for personal profit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a BC corporation with no employees, office, or business activity while routing FDA/CE consulting income to a low-tax jurisdiction through inflated management fees, royalties, or dividends, without meaningful transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA may recharacterize intercompany payments at arm's-length prices under section 247(2), impose the section 247(3) transfer pricing penalty of 10% of the net adjustment, deny treaty benefits under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, and reassess disguised dividends as taxable income. Directors may be assessed for unremitted source deductions and withheld Part XIII taxes under section 227.1.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for corporate withholding tax failures, are exposed to penalties for knowing participation in a sham conduit arrangement, and may face personal tax reassessments, civil fraud claims, and criminal prosecution for tax evasion if they acted in bad faith.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Preparing or approving fraudulent 510(k) summaries, falsifying biocompatibility or clinical evidence, issuing false CE technical files, or offering regulated medical device services without required professional or establishment credentials while charging fees through the BC corporation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under US FDA law, false 510(k) submissions may trigger civil money penalties, product seizure, import refusal, debarment, and criminal penalties including imprisonment. Under EU MDR 2017/745, misleading CE marking can result in market withdrawal, fines, and criminal prosecution in member states. Under Canada's Food and Drugs Act and Medical Devices Regulations, false or misleading device information is an offence punishable on indictment with fines and imprisonment. Fines or penalties imposed for regulatory convictions are not deductible for Canadian income tax purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate form does not shield a qualified individual who signs or submits a false regulatory declaration; directors who knowingly participate in medical device misrepresentation can face personal liability, professional disqualification, product recall costs, client indemnity claims, and criminal prosecution both abroad and in Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting wire or credit-card payments from clients where the source of funds is suspicious, failing to identify the ultimate beneficial owners of client entities, processing rapid pass-through payments, or failing to report a suspicious transaction to the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, administrative penalties may reach CAD 1,000,000 for a corporation per violation; laundering the proceeds of crime under section 462.31 of the Criminal Code is an indictable offence punishable by up to ten years imprisonment. The illegal fees remain taxable income, and unreported income from criminal activity is subject to ordinary tax, interest, and gross negligence penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly allow the corporation to process tainted funds can be prosecuted as parties or conspirators, face personal fines and imprisonment, and be subject to asset freezes, restraint orders, and travel bans in the course of a proceeds-of-crime investigation.
